assets.content:
Subject: When it’s time to plan next week’s posts
Preview text: If you use Insights, compare engagement rates before choosing the next batch.

Hi there,

A weekly test can stay small: schedule a few posts, let them publish, then use the results when choosing the next batch.

Buffer is a social media workspace for scheduling posts across connected channels and checking how they performed. On the Free plan, you can keep up to 10 posts scheduled per channel; each published post opens that slot again.

If you include Insights in the test, its Performance per Post table sorts published content by engagement rate. That gives you a concrete next step: decide which posts are worth repeating or building on when planning the following week. Free Insights also includes a Last 30 days view.

The official Insights guide shows how that performance comparison works. It won’t determine which metrics your particular channels report, but it can help you judge whether this review step is useful before signing up.

See how post comparison works →

- Buffer Customer Support

brief.promise: Buffer can give a small local business one simple weekly rhythm: schedule a few posts across its connected channels, then review basic post performance in Insights, with the Free plan’s limits stated plainly.
brief.orientation: Buffer is a social media workspace for scheduling posts across connected channels and checking how those posts performed.
brief.arc: Move from a concrete weekly routine, to the basic performance check that informs the next week, to an honest invitation to verify the Free plan’s fit and limits.
brief.sequence_rationale: Because the contract requires exactly one concise email, the message should demonstrate the complete queue-and-review loop rather than build a multi-email sequence. Lead with the weekly workflow, establish that Free includes 30 days of Insights and a sortable Performance per Post view, then disclose the 10-scheduled-posts-per-channel ceiling. The CTA points to official, read-only pages so the reader can resolve the earlier uncertainty about whether both parts of the workflow are available before signup.

emails.job: Help a cold prospect decide whether Buffer’s Free plan is suitable for testing one week of scheduling and basic post review.
emails.single_idea: Once a week, the reader can schedule a few posts for their connected channels, then return to Buffer’s Performance per Post view to see which posts earned more engagement; the Free plan permits up to 10 scheduled posts per channel and includes 30 days of Insights history.
emails.felt_need: A compact weekly routine for planning a few posts and learning from the results without turning social media into a larger project.
emails.mechanism: Queue a few posts for the coming week, let them publish, then sort the Performance per Post table by engagement rate before planning the next batch. On Free, keep the test within 10 scheduled posts per channel; published posts free those scheduling slots again.
emails.belief_shift: Before: it is unclear whether Buffer’s free entry covers both scheduling and a useful post-performance check. After: the reader sees a specific weekly test they can run within the disclosed 10-post-per-channel scheduling limit and 30-day Insights history.
must_not_say: Do not presume the reader currently uses native posting, another scheduler, spreadsheets, or any particular workflow.
Do not promise follower, reach, engagement, revenue, or time-saving growth.
Do not call Free unlimited: it allows up to 10 scheduled posts per channel, with a slot reopening after publication.
Do not imply that every network reports identical metrics or that every connected channel supports the same analytics.
Do not broaden the email into AI, comment management, collaboration, reporting exports, or the full channel list.
Do not state or imply that every reader uses Insights. Present this integration conditionally (for example, 'If you use Insights...') unless the user-supplied campaign context establishes it.
emails.objection: Is the queue-and-review workflow actually available on Free, or does the useful analytics step require a paid plan?
emails.tone: Practical, encouraging, and transparent; concise rather than promotional.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the Free plan’s 10 scheduled posts per channel and 30-day Insights history are enough for a small weekly trial.
emails.next_step_value: The official page documents this verified fact: Insights includes a sortable Performance per Post table that ranks content by engagement rate.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the pages does not establish which metrics the reader’s particular social channels will report or whether Buffer fits their ongoing volume beyond the Free limits.
emails.subject_strategy: Present the concrete weekly queue-and-review routine, with a cue that the free limit is stated openly; avoid generic productivity claims or implied growth.

brief.voice_notes: Use Buffer’s plainspoken vocabulary: “queue,” “channels,” “Insights,” and “check in.” Keep the workflow tangible and the limit adjacent to the Free-plan invitation.
